Content attribution, ownership, and accuracy for curated articles are governed by the disclaimers published on each respective sub‑site. Anthology Atelier does not claim authorship or copyright over curated material and provides its collections for educational and archival purposes.
For full details, please refer to the Anthology4Tech Disclaimer.

title: Disclaimer

content:
Anthology Atelier and its sub‑sites curate publicly shared technology content from trusted sources such as LinkedIn. The goal is to preserve, organize, and present valuable insights in a clean, searchable, and continuously updated format.
What We Curate#Technology articles originally posted by their respective presenters Visual content such as diagrams, slides, and animated images Links to original posts for attribution and verification What We Do Not Do#We do not write or author the curated articles We do not claim ownership or copyright We do not modify the original content beyond formatting for readability We do not include comments or follow‑on discussions Why This Exists#Professionals often lose track of valuable posts buried in feeds. Anthology solves this by:
Providing a permanent, organized archive Offering a subscriber‑only index of curated content Allowing readers to explore topics without social‑media noise Notes & Requests#Anthology does not claim to include all available articles on any topic; we curate what we find Please report any duplicate material so we can adjust the archive accordingly Our vault currently contains 2,500+ articles collected over the past six months, increasing by 10–30 articles daily The initial launch will include 150–200 curated articles, with 150–200 added each month How Subscriptions Will Work#Subscribers will gain access to:
The full curated article index Monthly content drops Topic‑based collections Optional email notifications Attribution & Rights#All rights remain with the original presenters.
We provide curation only — not authorship.
For full details, see the Disclaimer.
